entities.name: Andy Warhol Museum of Modern Art
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Andy Warhol Museum of Modern Art in Medzilaborce, Slovakia — not to be confused with The Andy Warhol Museum in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania — is a small but culturally significant institution in the village where Andy Warhol's Ruthenian (Rusyn) parents, Andrej and Júlia Warhola, were born before emigrating to the United States in the early 20th century. The museum, founded in 1991 shortly after Slovakia's transition from communism, contains one of the largest Warhol collections outside of Pittsburgh, including original silkscreen prints, drawings, and personal memorabilia.

Andy Warhol (born Andrew Warhola, 1928-1987) was the son of Carpatho-Rusyn Greek Catholic immigrants from the village of Miková, near Medzilaborce, in what was then the Kingdom of Hungary (later Czechoslovakia, now northeastern Slovakia). His parents' Byzantine Greek Catholic faith shaped aspects of Warhol's art — some scholars argue his iconic imagery (repeated images of consumer goods, celebrity portraits) has roots in the Eastern Christian icon tradition of repetitive sacred imagery.

The museum in Medzilaborce represents Slovakia's reclamation of its connection to one of the 20th century's most important artists, establishing cultural heritage tourism in an otherwise economically peripheral region of eastern Slovakia near the Ukrainian border. The museum has become an unexpected pilgrimage site for Warhol enthusiasts worldwide, and its existence highlights the global diaspora connections of Central and Eastern European immigrant communities to major 20th-century American cultural figures.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Andy Warhol Museum of Modern Art in Medzilaborce — preserving the Rusyn roots of America's most important Pop artist, establishing unexpected cultural heritage tourism in eastern Slovakia, and illuminating Central European immigrant contributions to American culture — is a uniquely meaningful if small institution in the global network of cultural heritage.
